analysis:
Examined two changed files.

(1) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift, head line 82: capacityRefreshTick now awaits checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue() after inventory registration. Its implementation is not in this batch. If it can trigger a model load or restore admission, it must honour servingDrain (lifecycle/addonHold owners), refusingNewWork, the add-on hold (TB-012/T-059/A-018), nativeMiMoAllowsReclamation and the load gate. Otherwise it could load models beside running VMs or reopen admission during a drain. That contract is unverified, and integration should check it. Nothing else changed in the capacity publish path (head 88-352), including the prefix-cache snapshot at head 310-318 (T-041), which is unchanged.

(2) ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, head 4-7 and 103-128: the final drain barrier now waits up to drainReconnectGrace (10s, capped by finishDeadline) for a registered connection. It sends acknowledgeDrain only when connected. If the session is still down and nothing was acknowledged, the drain reports .drained (sessionDown) rather than timedOut. This still requires nativeOwnersDrained and lifecycleRemaining==0. stopAppAttestWorkerAndWait still gates every outcome, and a worker that has not retired still yields timedOut. The --force semantics are unchanged. The safety claim rests on the comment that a disconnect cancels accepted work and the outbound path buffers nothing. That means no terminal or usage messages are lost by declaring drained. CoordinatorClient buffering and cancel-on-disconnect behaviour is not supplied. If the outbound path does queue usage or terminal frames for replay on reconnect, shutdown could drop them. That would be a billing and accounting loss on the provider side, with no consumer data exposure. One edge case: sessionDown can be set even after finishDeadline has passed with lifecycleRemaining==0. The base reported timedOut there; this is benign for confidentiality.

No encryption, attestation or authorization (TB-011/T-053) code changed in these units. No concrete regression was identified. Deeper review is requested for checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue and for the buffering contract behind CoordinatorClient.hasRegisteredConnection and acknowledgeDrain.
